title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_1LD1RA_1LB1LD_1RC0RC_---0LD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_1LD1RA_1LB1LD_1RC0RC_---0LD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of numbers that each sweep translates between two codes: runs 1^(3k+2) separated by single 0s when the head is at the right end, runs 1^(3a+1) separated by 0^(3b+2) when it is at the left end. The numbers themselves look irregular. Measured, not proved. Halting needs F on a 0, entered only from B on a 1; F has always found a 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 66,161 cells have been visited and 44,624 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: linear/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.303). Right of the start it grows in proportion to the step count (the head drifts steadily that way) (fitted exponent 0.891).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: Lean proves, for every count and every tape around, the shift rule of the leftward sweep: D turns a run of n 1s into n 0s as it crosses it, and so does B with two 1s travelling ahead of it, 3 steps per cell.

claims.title: Two codes for one list
claims.text: At the last right extension before 109 steps (step 911,093,030) the tape is 11,717 runs of 1s separated by single 0s, and 11,715 of the runs have length 3k+2 (up to 47 cells). At the last left extension (step 989,746,492) it is 6,128 runs of 1s, 6,115 of length 3a+1, separated by runs of 0s, 6,124 of length 3b+2, e.g. B>0 1^13 0^5 1^4 0^5 1^4 0^5 1^4 0^2 1^12 0^4 1^16 ….

claims.title: Never one step from a halt
claims.text: The machine halts when F reads a 0, and F is entered only from B reading a 1 (B1 → 0RF). In the first 3·10<sup>6</sup> steps B reads a 1 413,979 times, always with a 1 to its right.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The two codes are measured; the map a sweep makes on the list of numbers is not written down, and the numbers look pseudo-random, so this may be a chaotic machine.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine treats its tape as a list of numbers and rewrites the whole list on every sweep, switching between two ways of writing numbers in runs of 1s and 0s. This page shows the two codes and what is proved.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 66,161 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: One list, two codes
html: With the head at the right end, the tape is runs of 1s separated by single 0s, and nearly every run has length 2, 5, 8, 11, … (3k + 2):
With the head at the left end, it is runs of 1s of length 1, 4, 7, 10, … (3a + 1) separated by runs of 0s of length 2, 5, 8, … (3b + 2):
The machine translates the list from one code to the other on every sweep. The numbers in the list show no pattern that has been found.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The machine stops only in F reading a 0, and F is entered only from B reading a 1 (moving right). So a halt needs B on a 1 followed by a 0. In the first 3·106 steps B reads a 1 413,979 times and the next cell is always a 1. Open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.303). Right of the start it grows in proportion to the step count (the head drifts steadily that way) (fitted exponent 0.891).
After 109 steps the tape spans 66,161 cells (40,147 left of the start, 13,746 right), with a density of 1s of 0.674.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: list of numbers rewritten between two run-length codes
summary: Like its neighbour 1RB0RF_1LC1RD in this batch, every sweep rewrites the whole tape between two codes for a list of numbers: at the right end it is runs 1^(3k+2) separated by single 0s, at the left end runs 1^(3a+1) separated by 0^(3b+2); the numbers look irregular.
